ai_checks.proposal: Ask whether taking one algebra set first could change the second score, independent of music.
ai_checks.title: Check the order effect
ai_checks.why_review: A paired design still needs order and carryover controls.

ai_checks.proposal: Verify that quiet-condition and music-condition items have comparable difficulty before interpreting the difference.
ai_checks.title: Check whether the algebra sets match
ai_checks.why_review: Unequal item difficulty could create the apparent accuracy gap.

ai_checks.proposal: Keep the 4.2 percentage-point difference descriptive rather than translating it into effectiveness or causality.
ai_checks.title: Keep the wording bounded
ai_checks.why_review: A small descriptive sample difference does not establish a general effect.

capsule.evidence_summary: Twelve invented student IDs have paired scores: 78 of 120 correct in quiet and 83 of 120 with instrumental music.
limitations: No real students, class, school, audio, consent process, or experiment exists.
The 4.2 percentage-point difference is descriptive and has no significance or causal interpretation.
Order effects, item equivalence, prior ability, and classroom conditions are not established.
AI proposals are review prompts, not evidence.
capsule.title: Music and algebra accuracy — synthetic review capsule

summary.inference_notice: Descriptive difference only. No significance, causal, population, or effectiveness conclusion is supported.

drift_alarm.plain_reason: The new wording claims improvement for all students. This invented one-class sample supports only a small descriptive difference.
drift_alarm.supported_claim: In this synthetic class sample, algebra accuracy was slightly higher during the instrumental-music condition.
drift_alarm.unsupported_claim: Background music improves algebra performance for all students.

phrase_findings.note: A descriptive difference is not a causal estimate.
One invented class cannot support this population claim.
Accuracy is the measured synthetic outcome.

project.notice: Invented one-class dataset for product demonstration. It is not research evidence and describes no real students.
project.question: Does background instrumental music affect algebra accuracy for students in one high-school class?
project.title: Synthetic study: background instrumental music and algebra accuracy

repair.alternative: The synthetic one-class difference suggests a question for a separately approved study; it does not establish that music improves performance.
repair.before: Background music improves algebra performance for all students.
repair.reason: Both options remove the unsupported causal and all-students claims.
repair.recommended: In this synthetic class sample, algebra accuracy was slightly higher during the instrumental-music condition.
